title: Choose the Dialog API
prompt:
Northwind needs a Dialog. Known uses so far: a delete confirmation (title, sentence, two buttons), a driver-assignment form with a searchable list, a route preview with a map and a side panel, and a marketing newsletter sign-up. Four API proposals arrived. Pick the one you would approve.

```tsx
// A
<Dialog title="Delete route?" body="…" confirmLabel="Delete" confirmVariant="danger"
        cancelLabel="Cancel" showSidePanel={false} onConfirm={…} />

// B
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>{anything}</Dialog>

// C
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <Dialog.Header><Dialog.Title>Delete route?</Dialog.Title></Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Body>…</Dialog.Body>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Button onClick={close}>Cancel</Button>
    <Button variant="danger" onClick={remove}>Delete</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog>

// D
// No shared Dialog: each team builds its own on top of the native <dialog> element.
```
hints: List how different the four known uses are. Which API absorbs a map with a side panel without new props?
Then ask which option still lets the system own focus handling, spacing and the title's accessible name.
explanation: Proposal C composes: the system owns the overlay, focus handling, spacing and the title that names the dialog, while teams arrange header, body and footer content freely. A works for the delete confirmation and turns into prop explosion by the second use case. B is flexible but gives up structure, so every team re-solves titles, spacing and footers differently. D throws away the system's accessibility work entirely. A small configured `ConfirmDialog` can later be built on top of C for the most common case.

props.text: A: one Dialog configured entirely through props.
props.why: It fits the confirmation and fails the map preview; every new use becomes another prop such as `showSidePanel`.

children-only.text: B: a Dialog that renders whatever children it receives.
children-only.why: Maximally flexible, but the system no longer owns titles, spacing or footers, so dialogs drift apart again.

compound.text: C: a compound Dialog with Header, Title, Body and Footer pieces.
compound.why: Correct. It covers all four uses while the system keeps control of structure, styling and accessibility.

per-team.text: D: no shared component; teams use the native `<dialog>` element directly.
per-team.why: The native element is a good foundation for the system's Dialog, but leaving every team to style and label it recreates the inconsistency the system exists to remove.
